title: Chapter 52: Supreme Courage 2
content:
Chapter 52

Supreme Courage 2

Lan Wangji kept his gaze fixed straight ahead, tone flat. "It is nothing."

"Come on, aren't we practically old friends by now?" Wei Wuxian teased. "Why the cold shoulder? You won't even spare me a glance. Is your leg really alright?"

"We are not close."

Wei Wuxian spun on his heel and started jogging backward, forcing his grinning face right into Lan Wangji's line of sight. "Look, if something's wrong, don't play the hero. Did you hurt it, or is it broken? When did this happen?"

He was just winding up to offer, 'Want me to carry you?' when a sudden, sweet floral fragrance drifted past his nose. Wei Wuxian glanced over his shoulder toward the head of the path, his eyes lighting up instantly.

Seeing him abruptly shut his mouth, Lan Wangji’s eyes followed his gaze. A cluster of young maidens was walking together just ahead. The girl in the center wore a soft rose-tinted overcoat beneath a translucent gauze robe. Caught by the mountain breeze, the airy silk billowed around her, framing an undeniably striking silhouette.

And Wei Wuxian was staring directly at that back.

One of the girls chuckled playfully, "Mianmian, this sachet of yours really works wonders! Ever since I clipped it on, not a single bug has dared come near me. It smells wonderful, too—one breath and my whole head feels clear."

The maiden called Mianmian had a voice that lived up to her moniker—soft, sweet, and delicately airy: "It’s packed with finely shredded herbs; they serve quite a few purposes. I have a few spares on me—does anyone else want one?"

Before she could finish, Wei Wuxian blew over like a gust of rogue wind. "Mianmian, save one for me!"

The girl flinched in surprise. Catching the unfamiliar male voice cutting in out of nowhere, she turned around, revealing a delicate, lovely face framed by a startled scowl. "Who are you? And who gave you permission to call me Mianmian?"

Wei Wuxian beamed back. "I heard everyone calling you Mianmian, so I just figured that was your name. What, is it not?"

Lan Wangji watched the spectacle with icy detachment, while Jiang Cheng, witnessing another inevitable outbreak of shameless flirting, rolled his eyes so hard they nearly stuck in the back of his head.

Flushing crimson, Mianmian snapped, "You're not allowed to call me that!"

Wei Wuxian replied smoothly, "Why not? Tell you what: give me your real name, and I'll stop calling you Mianmian. Deal?"

"Why should I tell you just because you asked?" she countered. "Before demanding someone else's name, shouldn't you introduce yourself first?"

Wei Wuxian chuckled, "My name is easy enough. Keep it close to your heart: you can call me 'Yuandao'."

Mianmian silently turned the name 'Yuandao' over in her head a couple of times, struggling to recall any noble clan bearing a young master by that moniker. Yet judging by his sharp looks and effortless swagger, he hardly seemed like an obscure nobody. Catching the mischievous smirk tugging at the corners of his lips, she frowned, utterly baffled.

From the side, Lan Wangji’s icy murmur cut through the air: "A cheap play on words."The realization struck her like a bolt of lightning: Mianmian si yuandao—a famous poetic line meaning 'endless longing for one far away'. He was turning her name into a flirtatious pun, claiming she was longing for him! Stamping her foot in mortification, she fumed, "Who's longing for you?! Shameless!"

The surrounding maidens dissolved into giggles, chiming in playfully: "Wei Wuxian, you really have no shame at all!"

"I've never met anyone so insufferable!"

"Here, let me tell you, her real name is—"

Mianmian grabbed their sleeves, dragging them away in a fluster. "Let's go, quickly! Don't you dare tell him a thing!"

Wei Wuxian cupped his hands, shouting after them, "Leaving is fine, but at least toss me a sachet! Ignoring me? Not giving it up? If you don't give it to me, I'll just ask around until someone spills your name! Someone's bound to crack..."

Before the sentence cleared his lungs, a colorful pouch came hurtling out of the crowd, smacking squarely into his chest. Wei Wuxian clutched his heart with an exaggerated wince of heartbreak, before effortlessly hooking the silk string around his finger, spinning the sachet into a blur as he sauntered back to Lan Wangji with an unrepentant grin.

Catching the storm clouds gathering on Lan Wangji’s brow, he laughed, "What's that look for? Right, where were we before we got interrupted? Oh, right—how about I carry you on my back?"

Lan Wangji looked at him with unwavering, chilly stillness. "Are you this frivolous and wanton with everyone you meet?"

Wei Wuxian paused, stroking his chin in mock contemplation. "Pretty much, yeah."

Lan Wangji’s lashes lowered. After an agonizing silence, he ground out through clenched teeth: "...Reckless!"

The two syllables dripped with a visceral, biting frustration. Deciding Wei Wuxian wasn't even worth another glare, Lan Wangji forced his stride to quicken, limping forward.

Seeing him stubborn to a fault, Wei Wuxian quickly relented. "Alright, alright! You don't have to push yourself. I'll get out of your hair." Taking long strides, he caught up to Jiang Cheng.

Unsurprisingly, Jiang Cheng didn't have a kind face waiting for him either, spitting coldly, "You are utterly pathetic."

Wei Wuxian nudged him. "You're not Lan Zhan, so stop copying his vocabulary. What crawled up his ass today anyway? His face looks even sourer than usual. What happened to his leg?"

Jiang Cheng scoffed, "You actually have the luxury to worry about him? Look after your own neck first! Who knows what kind of cursed cave that idiot Wen Chao is driving us to find in Mount Muxi, or what deranged stunt he's pulling this time. Let's just hope he doesn't shove us to the frontlines as meat shields like he did with that tree beast."

A nearby disciple leaned in, keeping his voice to a hushed murmur. "You can hardly blame his mood. Cloud Recesses was put to the torch last month—haven't you heard?"

Wei Wuxian’s eyes went wide. "Burned?!"

Having caught wind of the rumors over the past few days, Jiang Cheng wasn't as shocked, asking grimly, "The Wen Clan did it?"

"You could say that," the disciple whispered. "Or rather... they forced the Lan Clan to burn it themselves. Wen Xu, the eldest son, marched on Gusu, slapped some fabricated crime on the Sect Leader's head, and coerced the Lan Clan into torching their own ancestral estate—calling it 'cleaning house for a fresh start.' More than half of the Cloud Recesses and the surrounding mountains went up in smoke. Centuries of celestial heritage, reduced to ashes. The Sect Leader was grievously wounded; no one even knows if he's still alive. A tragedy..."

Wei Wuxian’s jaw tightened. "Does Lan Zhan’s leg have something to do with that?"

"Of course it does," the boy replied. "The first building Wen Xu ordered them to torch was the Library Pavilion, barking that anyone who hesitated would pay dearly. Lan Wangji stood his ground and refused; Wen Xu's thugs swarmed him and broke his leg on the spot. He hadn't even begun to recover before he was dragged out here for this circus!"

Wei Wuxian pieced the last few days together in his head. Aside from enduring Wen Chao’s daily verbal lashings, Lan Wangji had barely moved. He spent every hour either standing rigid or sitting in dead silence. Given his obsessive devotion to martial decorum, he would rather die than let his enemies see him limp.

Catching Wei Wuxian instinctively drifting back toward Lan Wangji, Jiang Cheng hauled him back by the collar. "What are you doing now?! You still dare poke that bear? Are you actively courting death?!"

"I'm not trying to mess with him," Wei Wuxian hissed. "Look at that leg! Hiking non-stop through these crags has clearly aggravated the fracture to the point where he can't even hide it anymore. If he keeps walking on it, he's going to cripple himself for life. I'm going to carry him."

Jiang Cheng tightened his grip, snapping, "You're not even friends! Can't you see how much he despises your guts? You want to carry him? He wouldn't let you within three paces of him!"

Wei Wuxian shrugged. "So what if he hates me? I don't hate him. I'll just swoop in and hoist him up—what's he going to do, strangle me from my shoulders?"

Jiang Cheng's voice dropped, laced with a hard warning: "We can barely keep our own heads above water, and you're running around playing the righteous savior for outsiders?"

Wei Wuxian looked him dead in the eye. "First off, he's not an outsider. Second... someone has to step up."

Before the argument could escalate, a Wen attendant stormed over, barking, "Cut the whispering! Watch yourselves!"

Trailing behind the guard walked a glamorous young woman: Wang Lingjiao, one of Wen Chao’s personal retinue. What 'personal retinue' actually meant was an open secret to everyone present. Originally a maidservant serving Wen Chao’s legal wife, she’d weaponized her pretty face and batting eyelashes to climb straight into her master's bed. With one person rising to power, all her kin followed suit; nowadays, an upstart 'Yingchuan Wang Clan' had mysteriously clawed its way into the ranks of the sect rosters.

Lacking the spiritual core to wield a proper sword, she carried a slender iron branding iron in her grip. Every Wen enforcer was equipped with one—no fire pit required; a single touch against bare flesh burned a blisteringly agonizing mark straight into the skin.

Twirling the brand with smug arrogance, Wang Lingjiao sneered, "Young Master Wen ordered you to scour the mountain for the cavern entrance. What are you two slacking off and muttering about?"

To think a climbing maidservant had the audacity to strut and look down on noble heirs like dirt—the sheer absurdity of the times left both boys torn between disgust and grim disbelief.

Right then, a shout echoed through the brush: "Found it!"

Wang Lingjiao dropped them instantly, sprinting toward the clearing with a shrill cry of delight: "Young Master Wen! It's here! We found the entrance!"

It was a cleverly concealed fissure nestled at the roots of an ancient banyan tree so massive it would take three men to wrap their arms around it. The reason it had eluded them was twofold: the mouth was barely five feet across, and a dense, tangled net of ancient roots and creeping vines had woven a barrier across the opening, buried beneath layers of rotting loam and gravel.

Hacking through the fibrous roots and scraping away the damp muck, a gaping, pitch-black maw was laid bare to the daylight.

The subterranean chasm plunged straight into the bowels of the earth, venting a draft of bone-chilling air that made their hairs stand on end. Tossing a loose pebble down the drop, it vanished into the abyss without so much as an echo.

Wen Chao beamed with manic excitement. "This is definitely it! Move! Get down there, all of you!"

Jin Zixuan finally snapped, demanding in an icy tone, "You dragged us all the way out here claiming we were hunting a beast. What kind of monster are we dealing with? If you brief us on its nature, we can coordinate our defenses and avoid getting blindsided like last time."

Wen Chao sneered, "Brief you?"

He drew himself up, pointing an arrogant finger first at Jin Zixuan, then stabbing it back against his own chest. "How many times do I have to drill this into your thick skulls before it sticks? Don't get ahead of yourselves. You lot are nothing more than pawns under my command; I am the one issuing orders. I don't need advice from my underlings. I am the sole strategist, I am the commander, and I am the only one who will tame this beast!"

He hammered on the words 'only one' with sickening, unhinged hubris, coming across as both repulsive and laughable.

Wang Lingjiao chimed in sharply, "Didn't you hear Young Master Wen?! Get down there, now!"

Standing at the vanguard, Jin Zixuan swallowed his boiling fury. Gathering his robes, he grabbed hold of a thick, gnarled vine and vaulted straight into the yawning dark without a second thought.

For once, Wei Wuxian resonated with the young master completely. Whatever horrors were waiting at the bottom of that pit, facing a feral beast was leagues better than staring at Wen Chao’s greasy face. Sparing that disgusting pair another second of attention was practically begging for an impulse to drag them down to hell together.

Following Jin Zixuan’s lead, the rest of the disciples filed into the abyss one by one.

Stripped of their spiritual swords, the captive heirs had no choice but to climb down hand over hand. The tangled vines clinging to the damp rock walls were as thick as an infant’s forearm and held up under their weight. Rapelling slowly down the drop, Wei Wuxian silently tracked the distance.

They descended nearly three hundred feet before their boots finally touched solid stone.

Wen Chao hollered down from the rim a few times; once he was certain the bottom was clear, he hopped onto his flying sword, slung an arm around Wang Lingjiao’s waist, and glided down in lazy comfort. Moments later, his squad of enforcers and retainers dropped onto the cavern floor.

Jiang Cheng murmured under his breath, "Let's pray whatever he's hunting isn't an absolute nightmare. Who knows if this pit has another exit; if a beast goes berserk down here, climbing that vine will take too long—it might snap under our weight. We'd have zero escape route."

The grim reality weighed on everyone's chest, gazes drifting up toward the pinprick of pale daylight hundreds of feet above.

Stepping off his blade, Wen Chao barked, "What are you standing around staring for?! Do I need to wipe your noses too? Move!"

Herded like cattle, the boys were driven deeper into the subterranean gloom.

Needing them to scout the path ahead, Wen Chao ordered his guards to toss them a few torches. The cavern ceiling soared impossibly high, swallowing the torchlight in vast shadows. Tracking the hollow echoes of their footsteps, Wei Wuxian estimated they were several hundred feet beneath the mountain's crust.

Keeping their senses wound tight, the vanguard pushed through the cavern for an unknown stretch of time until the path opened onto an immense subterranean lake.

Had this body of water sat beneath the open sky, it would easily qualify as a sweeping lake. The water was pitch-black, broken up by dozens of jagged stone islands jutting from the surface.

And beyond the shore, the path dead-ended completely.

With the trail running out and their quarry nowhere in sight—not even leaving behind a footprint or a scent—dread coiled tight in everyone's chest.

Denied his glorious hunt, Wen Chao’s temper flared. Spitting curses, a sudden 'stroke of brilliance' struck him: "Grab someone, string them up from a stalactite, and drain some blood. That'll lure the beast out."

Feral beasts were universally driven mad by the scent of fresh blood; a helpless living bait dangling over the water would draw it out in seconds!

Wang Lingjiao caught the cue instantly, raising her brand to point at a petite silhouette: "Her! Use that one!"

The finger was pointed straight at Mianmian. Stunned, the girl froze in absolute disbelief. The selection looked arbitrary, but Wang Lingjiao had been nursing this grudge for days. With almost all the hostage disciples being young men, Wen Chao’s lecherous eyes naturally lingered on the few maidens present. Mianmian was remarkably pretty, and Wen Chao had already groped her a few times; though she’d swallowed the humiliation in silence, Wang Lingjiao had seen every glance and burned with jealous spite.

The moment Mianmian processed the order, panic took over and she stumbled backward. Seeing who had been singled out, Wen Chao hesitated, mourning the fact that he hadn't bedded the girl yet. "Her? Pick someone else."

Wang Lingjiao pouted, whining with exaggerated hurt, "Why switch? Did my pick strike a nerve? Are you going soft on her?"

That flirtatious whine melted Wen Chao’s spine on the spot. Looking at Mianmian’s simple robes, she clearly wasn't a direct heir—an ordinary guest disciple at best. Using her as disposable bait wouldn't trigger a political backlash from any prominent clan. He grinned lazily, "Nonsense, why would I care about her? Whatever you say, Jiaojiao—you call the shots!"

Knowing that being strung up meant certain death, Mianmian scrambled to hide. But wherever she ran, the surrounding disciples parted like the sea, dodging her like a plague. Wei Wuxian tensed to move, but Jiang Cheng clamped down on his wrist with an iron grip. Desperate, Mianmian spotted two silhouettes standing firm like stone pillars and dove behind their backs, trembling violently.

Those two were Jin Zixuan and Lan Wangji.

The Wen enforcers stepping forward with cords barked, "Out of the way!"

Lan Wangji didn't even blink.

Seeing defiance brewing, Wen Chao’s voice chilled. "What are you two loitering for? Don't understand human speech? Or are you playing the heroic white knights?"

Jin Zixuan arched an arrogant brow, his voice dripping with venom: "Haven't you had enough? Using us as meat shields wasn't enough for you, and now you want to bleed an innocent girl as live bait?!"

Wei Wuxian was genuinely surprised: Look at that peacock... turns out the bastard actually has some spine.

Wen Chao leveled an accusatory finger at them. "Are you staging a mutiny?! I'm warning you: my patience has worn paper-thin. Tie that little wench up and hang her over the water right this second, or not a single disciple from your clans walks off this mountain alive!"

Jin Zixuan let out a cold sneer, refusing to budge. Lan Wangji stood equally deaf to the threat, calm as an ancient well.

However, a Gusu Lan guest disciple standing nearby had been trembling violently beneath the weight of Wen Chao's threats. Breaking under the pressure, the boy lunged forward, grabbing Mianmian’s shoulder to bind her. Lan Wangji’s brow snapped into an icy scowl; with a lightning palm strike, he sent the traitor flying into the rocks.

He didn't utter a word, but the towering, majestic fury in his gaze spoke loud and clear: For the Gusu Lan Clan to harbor scum like you is an absolute disgrace!

The disciple clutched his bruised shoulder, shrinking back into the shadows, unable to meet his peers' disgusted stares. Wei Wuxian murmured to Jiang Cheng, "Lan Zhan’s unbending pride... this is going to blow up."

Jiang Cheng clenched his fists white-knuckled.

In this damp hellhole, staying clean and walking away without bloodshed was officially off the table!

Wen Chao’s face contorted with murderous rage. "Treason! Cut them down!"

Dozens of Wen enforcers unsheathed gleaming steel, lunging toward Lan Wangji and Jin Zixuan. Standing behind Wen Chao, Wen Zhuliu kept his hands folded behind his back, making no move to intervene—clearly viewing the scuffle as beneath him. It was a fair assessment: two unarmed boys heavily outnumbered by seasoned swordsmen were already at a massive disadvantage. Exhausted by days of forced marches and with Lan Wangji hobbled by a fractured leg, they wouldn't last three minutes.

Watching his men overwhelm the pair, Wen Chao’s mood soared, spitting, "Defying me? Arrogant trash. Dogs like this deserve to be slaughtered."

An amused, lilting voice piped up from the flank: "Indeed! Scum who rely on family prestige to bully the weak and commit atrocities deserve nothing less than slaughter! In fact, their heads should be struck off and left for the world to spit upon, serving as a permanent warning to future generations!"

Wen Chao whipped around. "What did you say?!"

Wei Wuxian put on a face of innocent surprise. "Need me to run that back for you? Happy to help: scum who rely on family prestige to bully the weak and commit atrocities deserve nothing less than slaughter—sever their heads and leave them for ten thousand souls to spit on! Hear me loud and clear that time?"

Hearing the quote, Wen Zhuliu’s eyes flickered with sudden thought, casting a sharp look at Wei Wuxian.

Wen Chao roared, "How dare you spew such treasonous, deranged bullshit!"

Wei Wuxian’s lips curved, and an instant later, an unrestrained howl of laughter tore from his throat.

Under the stunned stares of the crowd, he leaned his weight against Jiang Cheng’s shoulder, laughing so hard he could barely draw breath: "Treasonous bullshit?! Look in the mirror, idiot! Wen Chao, do you even know whose words those are? Of course you don't! Let me enlighten you: those words were spoken by the revered founder of your very own clan, the legendary Wen Mao himself! You just called your own founding ancestor's sacred decree 'treasonous bullshit'! Bravo! Well said! Hahah!"

The Wen Clan Anthology of Virtues was choked with mundane, rambling quotes from past leaders, inflated with dizzying praise. Wei Wuxian had only skimmed two pages before feeling thoroughly nauseated, but that specific quote from Wen Mao had dripped with so much irony he had committed it to memory.

Wen Chao’s face flushed violently, cycling between scarlet and pale. Wei Wuxian pressed the knife in: "By the way, what was the penalty for insulting a Wen ancestor? Summary execution on the spot, wasn't it? Well then, congratulations—you're free to drop dead now."

Blinded by incandescent fury, Wen Chao drew his sword and lunged straight for him.

That reckless charge took him clean outside Wen Zhuliu’s protective perimeter!

Wen Zhuliu was primed to counter incoming ambushes, never anticipating his young master would break formation on his own; the sudden move left him half a step behind. And that fleeting lapse of sanity was the exact opening Wei Wuxian had been baiting. Smiling with predatory ease, Wei Wuxian’s hand shot out like lightning, disarming the blade and flipping the strike to take Wen Chao hostage in a single breath!

Locking an arm around Wen Chao’s throat, Wei Wuxian vaulted across the subterranean air, touching down onto a rocky outcropping in the center of the lake to put distance between himself and Wen Zhuliu. Pressing the cold steel of Wen Chao’s own sword against the captive's jugular, he warned, "Nobody twitch! Move an inch and I'll bleed your young master dry!"

Wen Chao shrieked at the top of his lungs, "Hold your fire! Don't move! DON'T MOVE!"

The disciples besieging Lan Wangji and Jin Zixuan froze instantly.

Wei Wuxian barked toward the shore, "Core-Melting Hand, that goes for you too! You know your sect leader's temper better than anyone: his precious son is in my hands. If he loses a single drop of blood, every soul in this cavern—including you—is going to pay with their life!"

Wen Zhuliu slowly lowered his hands, holding his ground.

Seeing the board temporarily locked down, Wei Wuxian opened his mouth to dictate terms—only for a violent tremor to rattle through the stone beneath his boots.

He snapped, on guard, "Jiang Cheng! Is it an earthquake?!"

Trapped deep beneath the earth, a cave-in would bury them alive or seal the exit forever.

Jiang Cheng hollered back, "No!"

Yet the tremors grew increasingly violent, the sword shivering against Wen Chao’s throat, pulling terrified wails from the captive.

Suddenly, Jiang Cheng roared across the water: "It's not an earthquake! The damn rock under your feet is moving!!!"

Wei Wuxian’s gaze dropped. It wasn't the cavern shaking—it was the jagged island he had landed on. The stone was shivering, slowly grinding upward, breaking higher and higher out of the black water.

A chilling realization struck him: this was no stone outcropping. It was a colossal, primordial behemoth sleeping beneath the abyss.

And he was standing directly atop the beast's shell!
